projects.tagline: 100% client-side in-browser RAG with Transformers.js ONNX embeddings, WebGPU LLM inference, and PDF grounding.
projects.short_description: A zero-backend client-side RAG application that extracts text from PDFs, builds an in-memory vector index, and generates cited answers using local WebGPU language models.
projects.long_description: Northstar RAG POC is a client-side Retrieval-Augmented Generation application operating entirely within the user's browser with zero backend infrastructure and zero external API calls. Preloaded with 21 operational policy documents from the fictional Northstar Urgent Care Cooperative (64 pages), the application extracts per-page text via PDF.js, splits corpus documents into sliding-window text chunks, generates 384-dimensional vector embeddings using Transformers.js ONNX models, and stores chunk vectors directly in contiguous Float32Array buffers in heap memory for instant linear dot-product similarity search. Answers are streamed by WebLLM with hardware-accelerated WebGPU execution—supporting dynamic hot-swapping between Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM2-1.7B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B—with an integrated semantic retrieval fallback when WebGPU is unavailable. Built-in developer inspection tools provide a live PDF canvas viewer with bounding box highlights, chunk inspector modal, similarity ranking explorer, raw prompt preview, and a 15-query evaluation benchmark containing guardrail abstention tests.

projects.short_description: A hand-written Rust neural network compiled to WebAssembly: forward pass, backprop, SGD, and a ~200-line protobuf encoder that exports ONNX—with every weight, gradient, and loss step rendered on screen.
projects.long_description: TROT (Transparent Rust ONNX Trainer) is a small neural network built to be inspected rather than trusted. The model, backpropagation, loss, and weight updates are plain Rust loops in trot-core—no ndarray, no autodiff—compiled to WebAssembly so training runs entirely in the browser with no server, Python, or install. Six panels expose the whole pipeline: train with selectable activations and optional L2, export a hand-encoded ONNX graph and verify it with an in-place onnxruntime-web round-trip, browse the deterministic generated corpus (including intentionally flipped labels), inspect the full W1/b1/W2 weight grids, read the last minibatch's gradients cell by cell, and trace a single prediction through z1, activation, z2, and sigmoid. The corpus is a deterministic function of seed and size over a fixed 50-token grammar, so there is no dataset blob, and every number on the page is generated live.

projects.tagline: A deterministic, no_std Minesweeper state machine shaped for reinforcement learning.
projects.short_description: An allocation-free 8x8 Minesweeper engine with seeded SplitMix64 boards, observation/action-mask tensors, configurable strikes, and a browser conformance harness.
projects.long_description: mine-sm packages Minesweeper as a tiny reinforcement-learning environment rather than a game. The no_std Rust crate uses a flat 64-cell bitboard with no heap and exposes a three-call API: build a board from a seed or an exact mine mask, apply Reveal/Flag actions, and read back a [f32; 64] observation plus a legal-action mask shaped for a neural network. Bomb placement uses a hand-rolled SplitMix64 PRNG and rejection sampling, so the same (seed, actions) sequence produces byte-identical games on Wasm and native x86/ARM. Rules are configurable between classic sudden death and multi-strike/shielded play, and the engine implements safe first reveal, zero-cell cascade, flag protection, and terminal-state masking. The live harness visualizes observations and masks, auto-plays winning and losing lines, and runs conformance checks against the Rust engine; the repo includes golden, proptest, and scenario suites plus a quickstart example and ONNX-policy-friendly tooling.

projects.tagline: Compiling bounded AI reasoning into static, deterministic instruction sets
projects.short_description: Compiled Domain Expertise (CDE) is an architectural specification that compiles bounded AI reasoning into a static, language-agnostic Domain Instruction Set, replacing runtime neural nets with a deterministic, sub-megabyte relational graph.
projects.long_description: CDE proposes severing knowledge acquisition from knowledge execution. At build time, high-capacity models operate offline as an empirical knowledge compiler (Empirical Knowledge Compilation, EKC) to explore a closed domain, extract candidate reasoning structures, and surface inferential dependencies. At runtime, only surviving validated structures execute after being lowered into a Domain Instruction Set (DIS). The Quantized Semantic Bottleneck Architecture (QSBA) uses an hourglass topology that decouples continuous, high-dimensional linguistic transducers from a discrete, integer-only core, targeting exact attribution, loud syntax checks, and microsecond execution on standard CPUs within a sub-megabyte budget. The repo includes the specification, a CCPA reference instance (QSBC), an algebra domain with an ingest/review workbench (FastAPI backend + React frontend), supporting dialogues, docs, and generated slide decks.

projects.long_description: Heron's Fountain is an interactive, zero-dependency browser-based 2D simulation of the classical hydraulic apparatus described by Hero of Alexandria. It models three fluid vessels—a top open basin, an active lower compression chamber, and an elevated discharge chamber—interconnected by two liquid conduits and an isothermal shared-air tube (P2). As water drops through gravity intake P1, it seals the lower chamber and compresses the trapped gas volume according to polytropic PV relations. The resulting pneumatic head forces fluid through nozzle pipe P3, launching an arcing ballistic droplet stream into the basin. Features include dynamic chamber elevation inversion (swapping elevations and reversing flow paths), automated siphon triggers (jet velocity, flow rate, receiver fill percentage, cycle duration, and settled equilibrium), real-time gauge pressure telemetry (+kPa), and simulation time scaling up to 16×.

projects.short_description: A hand-written Rust neural network compiled to WebAssembly: forward pass, backprop, SGD, and a ~200-line protobuf encoder that exports ONNX—with every weight, gradient, and loss step rendered on screen.
projects.long_description: TROT (Transparent Rust ONNX Trainer) is a small neural network built to be inspected rather than trusted. The model, backpropagation, loss, and weight updates are plain Rust loops in trot-core—no ndarray, no autodiff—compiled to WebAssembly so training runs entirely in the browser with no server, Python, or install. Six panels expose the whole pipeline: train with selectable activations and optional L2, export a hand-encoded ONNX graph and verify it with an in-place onnxruntime-web round-trip, browse the deterministic generated corpus (including intentionally flipped labels), inspect the full W1/b1/W2 weight grids, read the last minibatch's gradients cell by cell, and trace a single prediction through z1, activation, z2, and sigmoid. The corpus is a deterministic function of seed and size over a fixed 50-token grammar, so there is no dataset blob, and every number on the page is generated live.

projects.tagline: Compiling bounded AI reasoning into static, deterministic instruction sets
projects.short_description: Compiled Domain Expertise (CDE) is an architectural specification that compiles bounded AI reasoning into a static, language-agnostic Domain Instruction Set, replacing runtime neural nets with a deterministic, sub-megabyte relational graph.
projects.long_description: CDE proposes severing knowledge acquisition from knowledge execution. At build time, high-capacity models operate offline as an empirical knowledge compiler (Empirical Knowledge Compilation, EKC) to explore a closed domain, extract candidate reasoning structures, and surface inferential dependencies. At runtime, only surviving validated structures execute after being lowered into a Domain Instruction Set (DIS). The Quantized Semantic Bottleneck Architecture (QSBA) uses an hourglass topology that decouples continuous, high-dimensional linguistic transducers from a discrete, integer-only core, targeting exact attribution, loud syntax checks, and microsecond execution on standard CPUs within a sub-megabyte budget. The repo includes the specification, a CCPA reference instance (QSBC), an algebra domain with an ingest/review workbench (FastAPI backend + React frontend), supporting dialogues, docs, and generated slide decks.

Creators can organize multi-platform video initiatives (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram), manage sponsor catalogs, formulate 30-second scripts via client-side AI providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Ollama), and synthesize multi-voice dialogue using in-browser neural Kokoro TTS with adjustable speech cadence, instant HTML5 waveform audio playback, and binary SQLite audio track archiving.

projects.short_description: A handcrafted, zero-build technical notebook rendering 34 in-depth hardware essays, interactive teardown schematics, and 5 specialized AI editorial personas with vanilla JS and Pico.css.
projects.long_description: tech.livive.net is an inspectable static publication notebook built with a strict zero-framework, zero-build-step philosophy. Powered by plain HTML, classless Pico.css, and client-side hash routing in vanilla JavaScript, it renders 34 deep technical essays across maker hardware, wearable acoustics, smart-home IoT, and modular computing. Each essay includes inspectable SVG schematics, PCB bus routing rules, and primary source citations. Its masthead introduces a multi-agent AI editorial board where 5 distinct personas (Forge, Ledger, Hearth, Timbre, and Compass) operate with transparent engineering beats, behavioral traits, and lab bench toolkits.
